config.theme: Sprint planning for a payments team at a fictional fintech
config.author: claude-opus-5-5 (Claude Code session)

cast.theme: Sprint planning for a payments team at a fictional fintech

personas.name: Tomas
personas.goals: A calm sprint with the tax tables done early
personas.hidden_agenda: Wants to protect the team from another crunch like January

personas.name: Yuki
personas.goals: Keep migrating companies at a steady pace
personas.hidden_agenda: Thinks the flaky tests are slowly poisoning morale

personas.name: Bea
personas.goals: Show progress on the migration to leadership
personas.hidden_agenda: Her quarterly target is the migration count

personas.name: Olu
personas.hidden_agenda: Has a plan for the flaky tests he hasn't pitched yet

agenda.title: Retro follow-ups
agenda.goal: Close or carry the open retro actions

agenda.title: Top of the backlog
agenda.goal: Pick the sprint goal from the migration and the tax tables

agenda.title: Capacity
agenda.goal: Fit the work to the holiday and the people

facts.statement: New tax tables must be live by April 1
Companies migrated to the new engine = 140

beats.summary: The three open actions; one closes, two carry
Migration vs tax tables; Bea overstates the migration count and Yuki corrects it
The holiday, the people and the test suite; Olu's runtime figure goes unchallenged

turns.speaker: Tomas
turns.text: Morning, everyone. Sprint seventeen. Let's start with the retro actions, there are three still open.

turns.speaker: Yuki
turns.text: The first one was mine, the deploy checklist. That's done, it's in the wiki now.

turns.speaker: Tomas
turns.text: Great, that one closes. The second was the on-call handover notes.

turns.speaker: Olu
turns.text: That's still open. Nobody really owned it.

turns.speaker: Tomas
turns.text: Would you be willing to take it this sprint, Olu?

turns.speaker: Olu
turns.text: Sure, I can take the handover notes.

turns.speaker: Bea
turns.text: And the third was the stakeholder demo. We never scheduled it.

turns.speaker: Tomas
turns.text: Let's leave the demo until the migration has something new to show.

turns.speaker: Bea
turns.text: That's fair. Leadership will ask, though.

turns.speaker: Yuki
turns.text: In practice, they ask every sprint.

turns.speaker: Bea
turns.text: Who's going to tell them it's postponed again?

turns.speaker: Tomas
turns.text: The backlog. Two big candidates: more migration batches, or the new tax tables.

turns.speaker: Bea
turns.text: The tax tables have a hard date. They have to be live by April first.

turns.speaker: Yuki
turns.text: And the payroll run on March twenty-eighth has to use the old tables, so we can't switch early.

turns.speaker: Olu
turns.text: So the switch has to happen in a three-day window. That's tight.

turns.speaker: Tomas
turns.text: How much of the tax work is already done?

turns.speaker: Yuki
turns.text: The rates are loaded. What's left is the rounding rules and the year-end edge cases.

turns.speaker: Bea
turns.text: And on the migration side, we've moved about two hundred companies so far.

turns.speaker: Yuki
turns.text: I think it's a hundred and forty. Two hundred is the number for the end of this sprint, if it goes well.

turns.speaker: Bea
turns.text: You're right, a hundred and forty. I was looking at the plan, not the actuals.

turns.speaker: Tomas
turns.text: Out of six hundred by June.

turns.speaker: Bea
turns.text: Which is why I want a migration batch in every sprint.

turns.speaker: Yuki
turns.text: In practice, I'd rather the sprint goal was the tax tables, with one small migration batch alongside.

turns.speaker: Olu
turns.text: What size is a small batch?

turns.speaker: Yuki
turns.text: Forty companies. The ones on the simplest pay schedules.

turns.speaker: Bea
turns.text: Forty is fine, as long as the batch happens.

turns.speaker: Tomas
turns.text: Okay. Sprint goal is the tax tables, plus one batch of forty simple companies.

turns.speaker: Bea
turns.text: I'll pick the forty companies and send Yuki the list by tomorrow.

turns.speaker: Tomas
turns.text: Capacity. We're four engineers, and there's one public holiday.

turns.speaker: Yuki
turns.text: Our average is thirty-one points. I'd plan to about twenty-seven with the holiday.

turns.speaker: Tomas
turns.text: Does anyone have time off planned?

turns.speaker: Olu
turns.text: I'm out on the Friday of the second week. Nobody else, as far as I know.

turns.speaker: Bea
turns.text: Then twenty-seven feels right.

turns.speaker: Olu
turns.text: The thing that eats our time is the test suite. It takes about half an hour for a full run.

turns.speaker: Yuki
turns.text: And then it fails on a flaky test and you run it again.

turns.speaker: Olu
turns.text: There are seventeen known flaky tests. I'd like to fix the worst five this sprint.

turns.speaker: Tomas
turns.text: Do the flaky tests fit under twenty-seven points with everything else?

turns.speaker: Bea
turns.text: It would have to come out of the migration batch, wouldn't it?

turns.speaker: Yuki
turns.text: Not necessarily. The tax work is mostly me and Kofi. Olu's capacity is separate.

turns.speaker: Tomas
turns.text: Then the five worst flaky tests go in as Olu's goal.

turns.speaker: Olu
turns.text: Thank you. That'll help everyone, honestly.

turns.speaker: Yuki
turns.text: Kofi had his baby on Saturday, by the way. A girl.

turns.speaker: Bea
turns.text: Oh, wonderful! He sent a photo to the channel, she's tiny.

turns.speaker: Olu
turns.text: He said nobody has slept since Friday.

turns.speaker: Tomas
turns.text: That reminds me, Kofi's on paternity leave from next week, so he's not in the capacity.

turns.speaker: Yuki
turns.text: Oh. Then the tax work is mostly me.

turns.speaker: Tomas
turns.text: Could someone pair with Yuki on the rounding rules?

turns.speaker: Olu
turns.text: I can. I know the rounding tests better than anyone.

turns.speaker: Tomas
turns.text: Dependencies and risks. What could stop us?

turns.speaker: Yuki
turns.text: The tax authority sometimes publishes corrections late in March. If that happens, we redo some of the work.

turns.speaker: Bea
turns.text: How often does that happen?

turns.speaker: Yuki
turns.text: Two of the last three years.

turns.speaker: Olu
turns.text: Nine open payroll bugs is the other risk. Some of them touch the same code as the tax tables.

turns.speaker: Tomas
turns.text: Are any of the nine likely to hit the March run?

turns.speaker: Olu
turns.text: One might. The overtime rounding one. I'd fix it before the run.

turns.speaker: Tomas
turns.text: Then the overtime rounding bug goes in first, before anything else.

turns.speaker: Yuki
turns.text: It would be good if someone kept an eye on the tax authority's website this month.

turns.speaker: Bea
turns.text: I'll set up an alert for their bulletin page this afternoon.

turns.speaker: Olu
turns.text: Should we tell support about the tax table switch, in case customers notice?

turns.speaker: Yuki
turns.text: Do we have a rollback plan if the new tables are wrong on April first?

turns.speaker: Tomas
turns.text: We keep the old tables deployed and switch back with a flag. That's how we did it last year. Okay, I think that's a plan. Thanks, everyone.
